subject: Intro & quick demo — Redwood fit for inference at Orchid AI
messages:
From: Alexa Rollins <alexa.rollins@orchidai.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in Redwood — quick demo request

Hi Ben,

I signed up for a trial on the Redwood site and wanted to reach out directly to see if we could set up a short demo next week. Quick context: we're building a semantic search + reranking layer for our ML-driven recommendation engine and are evaluating inference platforms that can meet sub-200ms tail latency for production traffic.

Estimated volume: ~1.2M queries/day, average 1.2k tokens per session (we usually batch multiple queries from the same session). Timeline: pilot in Q3, production by late Q3 / early Q4.

Questions for you before we book:
- Is Redwood used for low-latency production search workloads at our scale?
- Do you support per-route model pinning and KV/prefix caching?
- Any experience with data residency (we host in us-west and need controls for logs)?

Attaching a small usage sample (orchid-usage-sample.csv) so you can see our distribution. I'm available Mon/Tue afternoons next week (PDT).

Thanks,
Alexa
Alexa Rollins
Head of Platform Engineering, Orchid AI
alexa.rollins@orchidai.io
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — quick demo request

Hi Alexa — thanks for signing up and sending the sample, appreciate the context. Happy to set up a 30-minute demo and run through performance profiles that map to your traffic. A couple quick questions so I can tailor the session and loop in the right folks: 

1) Average tokens generated per query vs tokens in the prompt? (your sample helps but a quick ballpark is useful)
2) Do you expect many concurrent hot sessions (i.e., same user/session hitting model frequently)?
3) Any hard latency SLA for tail p95/p99? You mentioned sub-200ms tail — is that p95, p99, or both?
4) Are there security/compliance requirements beyond basic SOC2 (e.g., data residency contracts, customer-managed keys)?
5) Who will attend from your side (engineer/allows product), so I can invite the right Redwood folks (runtime / solutions engineer).

Proposed slots next week (PDT):
- Mon 7/13 2:00–2:30pm
- Mon 7/13 3:30–4:00pm
- Tue 7/14 1:00–1:30pm

If none of those work, tell me two windows that do and I'll send a calendar invite. I'll attach a short prep checklist and the agenda.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Alexa Rollins <alexa.rollins@orchidai.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Redwood — quick demo request

Hey Ben — thanks for the quick reply and the slots. Answers inline below.

1) Tokens: prompts average ~450 tokens, generated tokens usually ~220 on average (we often trim, but those are our means).
2) Concurrent hot sessions: yes — we have bursts tied to hourly batch jobs and also spikes during peak traffic; expect 2k–4k concurrent requests in bursts.
3) Latency: we need p95 < 200ms in our US-WEST region; p99 ideally < 350ms.
4) Compliance: SOC2 ok; we also need customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest (enterprise contract).
5) Attendees: Myself + Tom Berger (lead ML infra) + one product manager (TBD).

We can do Mon 7/13 3:30–4:00pm PDT — that works best. I'll attach a short notes file and the usage sample.

Thanks,
Alexa
